import pandas as pd

# Load the intermediate result after UNPIVOT operation
intermediate_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_47/intermediate_step1.csv"
df = pd.read_csv(intermediate_path)

# The schema of intermediate_step1.csv is:
# ['Country Name', 'Country Code', 'Year', 'Rural Value', 'Electricity Value']
# But 'Year' column is likely numeric (int or float), while target expects string.
# Convert 'Year' to string to match target schema and avoid merge type conflicts.
df['Year'] = df['Year'].astype(str)

# The target schema is:
# ['Country Name': string, 'Country Code': string, 'Year': string, 'Rural Value': string, 'Electricity Value': string]
# Convert 'Rural Value' and 'Electricity Value' to string as well, preserving NaNs as 'nan' strings or empty strings.
# To keep NaNs as NaN (missing), convert to string but keep NaNs as is by using .astype(str) then replacing 'nan' with pd.NA.
# But target examples show NaN as actual NaN, so better keep them as NaN.
# So convert numeric columns to string but keep NaNs as NaN:
df['Rural Value'] = df['Rural Value'].apply(lambda x: str(x) if pd.notna(x) else pd.NA)
df['Electricity Value'] = df['Electricity Value'].apply(lambda x: str(x) if pd.notna(x) else pd.NA)

# Save the final target table to the specified path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_47/target_multisource.csv"
df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read sources with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_47/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_47/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# UNPIVOT Source3_47_0
source0_unpivot = source0.melt(
    id_vars=['Country Name', 'Country Code', 'Indicator Name', 'Indicator Code'],
    var_name='Year',
    value_name='Value'
)

# UNPIVOT Source3_47_1
source1_unpivot = source1.melt(
    id_vars=['Country Name', 'Country Code', 'Indicator Name', 'Indicator Code'],
    var_name='Year',
    value_name='Value'
)

# FILTER Source3_47_0 for Rural population indicator
source0_filtered = source0_unpivot[
    source0_unpivot['Indicator Name'] == 'Rural population (% of total population)'
].copy()

# Rename Value to Rural Value
source0_filtered.rename(columns={'Value': 'Rural Value'}, inplace=True)

# FILTER Source3_47_1 for Electricity access indicator
source1_filtered = source1_unpivot[
    source1_unpivot['Indicator Name'] == 'Access to electricity (% of population)'
].copy()

# Rename Value to Electricity Value
source1_filtered.rename(columns={'Value': 'Electricity Value'}, inplace=True)

# JOIN on Country Name, Country Code, Year
merged = pd.merge(
    source0_filtered[['Country Name', 'Country Code', 'Year', 'Rural Value']],
    source1_filtered[['Country Name', 'Country Code', 'Year', 'Electricity Value']],
    on=['Country Name', 'Country Code', 'Year'],
    how='outer'  # Use outer join to keep all data, including NaNs as in target examples
)

# Ensure columns order and types as target schema
final = merged[['Country Name', 'Country Code', 'Year', 'Rural Value', 'Electricity Value']]

# Convert all columns to string type as in target schema
final = final.astype(str)

# Write to target file
final.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_47/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
